The '''37th Academy Awards''' were held on April 5, 1965, to honor [[1964 in film|film achievements of 1964]]. The ceremony was produced by [[Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer|MGM]]'s [[Joe Pasternak]] and hosted, for the 14th time, by [[Bob Hope]].
 
The Best Picture winner, [[George Cukor]]'s ''[[My Fair Lady (film)|My Fair Lady]]'', was an adaptation of a 1956 [[My Fair Lady|stage musical of the same name]], which was itself based on [[George Bernard Shaw]]'s ''[[Pygmalion (1938 film)|Pygmalion]]'', which had been nominated for Best Picture in [[11th Academy Awards|1938]]. [[Audrey Hepburn]] was controversially not nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Actress|Best Actress]] for her starring role as [[Eliza Doolittle]];<ref name="Oscars '64 Notes">
{{cite book |last1=Wallechinsky |first1=David |last2=Wallace |first2=Irving |date=1975 |title=The People's Almanac |url=https://archive.org/details/peoplesalmanac00wall/page/842/mode/2up |location=Garden City, New York |publisher=Doubleday & Company, Inc. |page=843 |isbn=0-385-04060-1}}</ref>  the unpopularity of her replacing [[Julie Andrews]]—who had originated the role on Broadway, and who was seen by producer [[Jack L. Warner|Jack Warner]] as having lacked star quality<ref name="Oscars '64 Notes"/>—as well as the revelation that the majority of her singing was dubbed by [[Marni Nixon]] (which wasn't approved by Hepburn herself) were seen as the main reasons for the snub. This was said to have "split the committee into two camps, pro and con, for and against the two ladies", and even led to talk of a write-in campaign for Hepburn.<ref name="Oscars '64 Notes"/> Despite her having not been nominated, Hepburn was in attendance at the ceremony, with camera work playing up the tension between the two considerably.<ref name="Oscars '64 Notes"/> Andrews won the Best Actress Oscar, but ''My Fair Lady'' was said to have "made off awfully well, too."<ref name="Oscars '64 Notes"/>

The ceremony saw the first recipient of the [[Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling]], [[William J. Tuttle]] for ''[[7 Faces of Dr. Lao]]'', albeit as an [[Academy Honorary Award|Honorary Award]]; it would not become a competitive category until [[54th Academy Awards|1981]].

This year was the first in which three films received 10 or more nominations (repeated at the [[50th Academy Awards|50th]], [[92nd Academy Awards|92nd]] and [[96th Academy Awards]]), and the only time in Oscar history that three films received 12 or more nominations: ''[[Becket (1964 film)|Becket]]'' and ''[[My Fair Lady (film)|My Fair Lady]]'' each received 12, while ''[[Mary Poppins (film)|Mary Poppins]]'' received 13. Also, the five Best Director nominees corresponded to their films in the Best Picture category, for only the second occurrence throughout the era (1944–2008) in Oscar history, where the latter category was limited to five nominees only. Additionally, for the first time all Best Picture nominees received corresponding directing and writing nominations.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Keith |title=Oscar facts & figures |url=https://variety.com/2006/film/awards/oscar-facts-figures-1117918228/ |access-date=June 15, 2026 |work=Variety |date=February 21, 2006 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190605184741/https://variety.com/2006/film/awards/oscar-facts-figures-1117918228/ |archive-date=June 5, 2019 }}</ref>

''Becket'' tied the record set by ''[[Johnny Belinda (1948 film)|Johnny Belinda]]'' for most Oscars losses with 11 (both movies won 1 out of 12 nominations). It was later equalled by ''[[The Turning Point (1977 film)|The Turning Point]]'' in [[50th Academy Awards|1977]] (0 for 11), ''[[The Color Purple (1985 film)|The Color Purple]]'' in [[57th Academy Awards|1985]] (0 for 11), ''[[The Power of the Dog (film)|The Power of the Dog]]'' in [[94th Academy Awards|2021]] (1 for 12), and ''[[Emilia Pérez]]'' in [[97th Academy Awards|2024]] (2 for 13).

==Multiple nominations and awards==
{{Col-begin}}
{{Col-1-of-2}}
These films had multiple nominations:

* ''13 nominations:'' ''[[Mary Poppins (film)|Mary Poppins]]''
* ''12 nominations:'' ''[[Becket (1964 film)|Becket]]'' and ''[[My Fair Lady (film)|My Fair Lady]]''
* ''7 nominations:'' ''[[Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte]]'' and ''[[Zorba the Greek (film)|Zorba the Greek]]''
* ''6 nominations:'' ''[[The Unsinkable Molly Brown (film)|The Unsinkable Molly Brown]]''
* ''4 nominations:'' ''[[Dr. Strangelove|Dr. Strangelove, or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb]]'' and ''[[The Night of the Iguana (film)|The Night of the Iguana]]''
* ''3 nominations:'' ''[[Father Goose (film)|Father Goose]]''
* ''2 nominations:'' ''[[The Americanization of Emily]]'', ''[[A Hard Day's Night (film)|A Hard Day's Night]]'', ''[[Robin and the 7 Hoods]]'', ''[[Seven Days in May]]'', and ''[[What a Way to Go!]]''

{{Col-2-of-2}}
The following films received multiple awards.

* ''8 wins:'' ''[[My Fair Lady (film)|My Fair Lady]]''
* ''5 wins:'' ''[[Mary Poppins (film)|Mary Poppins]]''
* ''3 wins:'' ''[[Zorba the Greek (film)|Zorba the Greek]]''

{{Col-end}}
